author: Jeremy Goldstein
title: FIFA World Cup host region might have serial killer on the loose - NewsBreak
text:
By Jeremy Goldstein ,
1 hours ago The Mexican state of Jalisco will host four 2026 FIFA World Cup matches at the upcoming tournament. But the same region also may have a potential serial killer on the loose after the bodies of three women were found in an 11-day span in similar circumstances.
Jalisco is home to both Puerto Vallarta, a popular coastal tourist destination often flooded with Americans, and Guadalajara, the home of the Estadio Akron, a World Cup venue.
The Mexican state is one of the western hemisphere's more dangerous areas. Cartel-related violence erupted in the region in February after the murder of Nemesio Oseguera Cervantes, a powerful cartel boss. Rumors swirled about whether Mexico would lose the right to host the World Cup.

• Tom Brady awkwardly beaten to award by man he replaced for $375 million
Three mid-30s women with tattoos were found undressed in Puerto Vallarta, per a report corroborated by multiple sources. The case has yet to be formally classified as a serial killing due to the lack of total evidence.
“At the moment, the preliminary information does not indicate that they are linked,” prosecutors told Mexican outlet Reporte Diario .
President Claudia Sheinbaum vowed to deploy 100,000 members of the country's security force for the World Cup to protect foreign visitors.
“We are here … to tell everyone in Jalisco, all the people of Jalisco, that we are together, that we are working for peace, security and the well-being of the inhabitants of this beautiful state,” Sheinbaum said in March.
Estadio Acron is the local home of LIGA MX side C.D. Guadalajara, one of the nation's strongest teams. It will host four World Cup matches.
Those matches include: South Korea vs Czechia on June 11, Mexico vs South Korea on June 18, Colombia vs. DR Congo on June 23, and Uruguay vs Spain on June 26.

The Mexican national team enters the 2026 World Cup having not reached the quarterfinals since 1986, a tournament hosted on home soil.
Mexico lost seven consecutive Round of 16 matches from 1994 to 2018. El Tri failed to advance from the group stage at Qatar 2022, finishing third in a group that also featured Argentina, Poland, and Saudi Arabia.
The current Mexican national team is a veteran side led by familiar faces like striker Raul Jimenez, midfielder Edson Alvarez, and goalkeeper Guillermo Ochoa.
Tijuana midfielder Gilberto Mora, 17, adds a sprinkle of youth. The talented teen scored nine goals, including two on the road against the Los Angeles Galaxy in the League Cup as part of a breakout 2025 campaign.
